Why does the eye need tears?

The clear front of your eye has no blood vessels at all! So your tears carry food and oxygen to it instead, keeping your eye healthy.
copy.tl:
Bakit kailangan ng mata ang luha?

Ang malinaw na harap ng mata ay walang ugat ng dugo! Kaya ang luha ang nagdadala ng pagkain at oxygen dito para manatiling malusog ang mata.
copy.bis:
Ngano kinahanglan sa mata ang luha?

Ang matin-aw nga atubangan sa mata walay ugat sa dugo! Busa ang luha maoy nagdala og pagkaon ug oxygen niini aron magpabiling himsog ang mata.

copy.tl: Dahil patuloy na gumagalaw ang mga plato, iba ang anyo ng mapa ng Earth ngayon kumpara sa milyon-milyong taon na ang nakalipas — at magbabago pa ang mga kontinente!
copy.bis: Tungod kay padayon nga naglihok ang mga plato, lahi ang dagway sa mapa sa Earth karon kompara sa minilyon ka tuig nga milabay — ug mausab pa ang mga kontinente!

copy.tl: Alam mo ba na ang matatalim mong harapang ngipin ay gumagana tulad ng wedge? Hinihiwa at hinihati nito ang pagkain sa bawat kagat mo!
copy.bis: Nahibaw-an ba nimo nga ang imong hait nga atubangang ngipon molihok sama sa wedge? Gahiwa ug gibahin niini ang pagkaon sa matag imong kagat!

Which came first, the telegraph or the telephone?

The telegraph in 1844! It sent coded signals through a wire before the telephone that carries our voice was invented in 1876.
copy.tl:
Alin ang nauna, ang telegraph o ang telepono?

Ang telegraph noong 1844! Nagpadala ito ng mga code sa kable bago pa naimbento ang teleponong nagdadala ng boses noong 1876.

Hain ang nauna, ang telegraph o ang telepono?

Ang telegraph niadtong 1844! Nagpadala kini og mga code pinaagi sa kable sa wala pa ang telepono nga nagdala sa tingog niadtong 1876.

copy.en:
How did Galileo get such a close-up view of the Moon and stars?

Around 1609, Galileo used a telescope — a tool with lenses that makes far-away objects look bigger — to study the Moon, planets, and stars.
copy.tl:
Paano nakakita si Galileo ng malinaw na tingin sa Buwan at mga bituin?

Noong mga 1609, gumamit si Galileo ng teleskopyo — isang kagamitan na may lente na nagpapalaki sa malalayong bagay — para pag-aralan ang Buwan, mga planeta, at bituin.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagtan-aw ni Galileo og klaro sa Bulan ug mga bituon?

Niadtong mga 1609, migamit si Galileo og teleskopyo — usa ka himan nga adunay lente nga nagpadako sa layong butang — aron tun-an ang Bulan, mga planeta, ug bituon.

How do we see faraway stars and planets?

A telescope uses lenses or mirrors to gather light from faraway objects like stars and planets!

Gumagamit ang telescope ng lenses o mirrors para ipunin ang liwanag mula sa malalayong bagay tulad ng bituin at planeta!

Giunsa nato makita ang layo nga bituon ug planeta?

Naggamit ang telescope og lenses o mirrors aron tigumon ang kahayag gikan sa layo nga mga butang sama sa bituon ug planeta!

copy.bis: Magpadako ang teleskopyo sa hitsura sa layo nga mga butang! Mao nga ang mga planeta ug bulan morag mas dako ug mas duol kaysa makita sa mata lamang.

copy.bis: Ang teleskopyo magpakita og mas daghang bituon ug galaxy kaysa makita sa mata! Magtigom kini sa huyang nga kahayag gikan sa layo nga mga butang.

What is the difference between a telescope and a microscope?

A telescope is for seeing far-away things like stars, while a microscope is for very tiny things close up. They have opposite jobs!
copy.tl:
Ano ang pagkakaiba ng teleskopyo at mikroskopyo?

Ang teleskopyo ay para makita ang malalayong bagay gaya ng bituin, samantalang ang mikroskopyo ay para sa napakaliliit na bagay na malapit lang. Magkaibang gamit sila!
copy.bis:
Unsay kalainan sa teleskopyo ug mikroskopyo?

Ang teleskopyo alang sa pagtan-aw sa layo nga mga butang sama sa bituon, samtang ang mikroskopyo alang sa gagmay kaayo nga butang nga duol lang. Magkalahi ang ilang gamit!

copy.bis: Ang kalainan sa temperatura maghimo ug kalainan sa air pressure, kay ang init nga hangin mosaka ug magbilin ug lugar nga adunay mas diyutay nga air particles.

copy.tl: Ang terminal velocity ay ang pinakamabilis na bilis na naaabot ng nahuhulog na bagay! Para sa skydiver, ito ay halos 200 km/h.
copy.bis: Ang terminal velocity mao ang pinakapaspas nga katulin nga maabot sa nahulog nga butang! Para sa skydiver, mga 200 km/h kini.

Most worker termites can barely see, so they follow smell and chemical trails left by other termites to find food and their way home.

Paano nakakahanap ng daan ang mga bulag na anay?

Halos hindi nakakakita ang karamihan ng manggagawang anay, kaya sinusundan nila ang amoy at kemikal na bakas ng ibang anay para mahanap ang pagkain at daan pauwi.

Unsaon pagpangita og dalan sa buta nga mga anay?

Halos dili makakita ang kadaghanan sa trabahante nga anay, mao nga gisundan nila ang baho ug kemikal nga agi sa ubang anay aron makit-an ang pagkaon ug dalan pauli.

copy.en: In a termite colony, most termites are workers — only a few become soldiers, because guarding the nest takes far fewer termites than gathering food.
copy.tl: Kakaunti lang ang mga sundalong termite sa isang kolonya — mas marami ang manggagawa, dahil mas maraming termite ang kailangan para magtrabaho at magpakain kaysa magbantay.
copy.bis: Gamay ra ang mga sundalo nga termite sa usa ka kolonya — mas daghan ang trabahante, kay mas daghan ang gikinahanglan motrabaho ug mopakaon kaysa magbantay.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: people eat swarming termites
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to group animals according to the food they eat: plant eaters (herbivores), meat eaters (carnivores), and plant and meat-eaters (omnivores)
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses humans eating termites, not grouping animals by their food type (herbivore/carnivore/omnivore). It does not support the competency's classification skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: not only animals that benefit from a swarm
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe examples and explain how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet their basic needs
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions that both people and animals benefit from a termite swarm, but it does not explain how living things depend on one another or on the environment to meet basic needs. The dependency concept is only implied, not taught.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: people eat swarming termites
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: draw a simple food chain using living things from the Philippines and label them as herbivores, carnivores, and omnivores
assignedReviews.reason: The competency requires drawing a food chain using Philippine living things and labeling them as herbivores, carnivores, or omnivores. The card is about human consumption of termites in Africa and Asia, not a Philippine food chain, and no food chain or labels are provided.

copy.en:
Do people really eat termites?

In parts of Africa and Asia, people eat swarming termites, usually fried — they're rich in protein, so it's not only animals that benefit from a swarm.
copy.tl:
Kinakain ba talaga ng tao ang anay?

Sa ilang bahagi ng Africa at Asia, kinakain ng tao ang lumilipad na anay, kadalasan prinito — mayaman ito sa protina, kaya hindi lang hayop ang nakikinabang sa swarming.
copy.bis:
Nagkaon ba gyud og anay ang tawo?

Sa pipila ka bahin sa Africa ug Asia, gikaon sa tawo ang naglupad nga anay, kasagaran giprito — dato kini sa protina, mao nga dili lang mananap ang makabenepisyo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: using a special scent so they don't lose each other
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a specific termite behavior (following a scent) but does not teach the general characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). The scent-following could be interpreted as a response, but the card does not frame it as a characteristic of living things, nor does it mention growth or reproduction explicitly.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: hunting for a spot to dig
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe examples and explain how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet their basic needs
assignedReviews.reason: The card shows termites cooperating to find a nest site, which is a social interaction, but it does not explain how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet basic needs. The pair's cooperation is not framed as meeting basic needs, and the environment (nest spot) is only a location, not a resource dependency.

copy.en: After a male and female termite pair up, the female leads while the male follows close behind — using a special scent so they don't lose each other while hunting for a spot to dig.
copy.tl: Kapag nagpares na ang lalaki at babaeng anay, hawak ng babae ang unahan habang sumusunod ang lalaki — gamit ang espesyal na amoy para hindi sila mawalay habang naghahanap ng lugar na huhukayin.
copy.bis: Kung magtiayon na ang laki ug baye nga anay, ang baye mag-una samtang ang laki mosunod ug duol — gamit ang espesyal nga baho aron dili sila mawad-anay samtang nangita og dapit nga kalotan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It is the hormone from the testes that causes secondary male characteristics like a deeper voice and facial hair.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how different factors affect the solubility of a solute in a given solvent, such as heat
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes testosterone's role in male puberty, a biology topic. G7-M-10 requires demonstrating factors affecting solubility of a solute in a solvent, which is a chemistry/matter concept. There is no instructional support for solubility.

copy.en:
What does testosterone do in boys?

It is the hormone from the testes that causes secondary male characteristics like a deeper voice and facial hair.
copy.tl:
Ano ang ginagawa ng testosterone sa mga lalaki?

Ito ang hormone mula sa testes na nagdudulot ng secondary male characteristics tulad ng paglalim ng boses at pagtubo ng buhok sa mukha.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang gibuhat sa testosterone sa mga lalaki?

Kini ang hormone nga nagagikan sa testes nga nagpahinabo sa secondary male characteristics sama sa paglawom sa tingog ug pagtubo sa buhok sa nawong.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Texture is how something feels when you touch it
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: investigate the properties of ionic, covalent, and metallic substances, such as melting point, hardness, electrical and thermal conductivity
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines texture as a general tactile property (smooth, rough, soft, hard). G9-M-11 requires investigating properties of ionic, covalent, and metallic substances such as melting point, hardness, and electrical/thermal conductivity. Texture is not a property of these specific substance classes and provides no instructional support for the competency.

copy.en:
What does texture mean?

Texture is how something feels when you touch it, and it can be smooth, rough, soft, or hard!
copy.tl:
Ano ang ibig sabihin ng texture?

Ang texture ay kung paano nararamdaman ang isang bagay kapag hinawakan mo ito, at maaari itong smooth, rough, soft, o hard!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang gipasabot sa texture?

Ang texture mao kung unsa ang bation sa usa ka butang kung imong hikapon, ug kini mahimong smooth, rough, soft, o hard!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The eyepiece, also called the ocular, is the lens you look through, and it magnifies an object ten times (10x).
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to describe and illustrate the reflection of light using plane and curved mirrors and the refraction of light using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms with examples from everyday applications
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies the eyepiece as a lens that magnifies, but it does not describe or illustrate reflection or refraction of light, nor does it involve mirrors, prisms, or transparent blocks. It only names a microscope part and its magnification, which is not direct instruction for the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The eyepiece, also called the ocular, is the lens you look through, and it magnifies an object ten times (10x).
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided science activities to explore and describe sources of light, how it behaves or can be changed, and its uses in everyday situations
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a lens and magnification, but it does not explore sources of light, how light behaves or can be changed, or its everyday uses. It is a fact about a microscope eyepiece, not an activity or description of light behavior.

copy.en: The eyepiece, also called the ocular, is the lens you look through, and it magnifies an object ten times (10x).
copy.tl: Ang eyepiece, na tinatawag ding ocular, ay ang lens na tinitingnan mo, at pinalalaki nito ang isang bagay ng sampung beses (10x).
copy.bis: Ang eyepiece, gitawag usab nga ocular, mao ang lens nga imong gitan-aw, ug gipadako kini sa usa ka butang ug napulo ka pilo (10x).

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Negative feedback is the most common homeostatic mechanism
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that energy is something that can cause change including light, sound, and heat energy
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes negative feedback in homeostasis, a biological regulatory concept, and does not address energy as something that can cause change (light, sound, heat). It is unrelated to the competency.

copy.en: Negative feedback is the most common homeostatic mechanism because it constantly makes small corrections to keep your body stable all day long.
copy.tl: Ang negative feedback ang pinakakaraniwang homeostatic mechanism dahil patuloy itong gumagawa ng maliliit na pagwawasto para mapanatiling stable ang katawan sa buong araw.
copy.bis: Ang negative feedback mao ang labing komon nga homeostatic mechanism tungod kay padayon kini nga mohimo og gagmay nga mga pagtul-id aron magpabilin nga stable ang lawas sa tibuok adlaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Heat flows from the hotter object to the cooler one until their temperatures equalize.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the difference between heat and temperature
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes heat flow and thermal equilibrium but does not explain the difference between heat and temperature. It uses both terms without contrasting their meanings, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
What happens when hot and cold things touch?

Heat flows from the hotter object to the cooler one until their temperatures equalize. This is called thermal equilibrium!
copy.tl:
Ano ang nangyayari kapag nagkahipo ang mainit at malamig?

Dumadaloy ang init mula sa mas mainit papunta sa mas malamig hanggang maging pantay ang temperatura. Tawag dito ay thermal equilibrium!
copy.bis:
Unsay mahitabo kung maghikap ang mainit ug malamig?

Mobalhin ang init gikan sa mas mainit ngadto sa mas malamig hangtod magkapareho ang temperatura. Gitawag kini nga thermal equilibrium!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Solids, liquids, and gases all expand when heated!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe that particles are constantly in motion, have spaces between them, attract each other, and move faster as the temperature increases (or with the addition of heat)
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes macroscopic thermal expansion (gases expand most, solids least) but never mentions particles, their motion, spacing, attraction, or increased speed with temperature. It does not directly teach the particle-level description required by G7-M-3; it is only topically related to heat effects on matter.

copy.en:
Which expands the most when heated: solids, liquids, or gases?

Solids, liquids, and gases all expand when heated! But gases expand the most, while solids expand the least.
copy.tl:
Alin ang pinakamalaking lumalaki kapag pinainit: solid, likido, o gas?

Lumalaki sa init ang mga solid, likido, at gas! Pero pinakamalaki ang paglaki ng gas, at pinakamaliit naman ang solid.
copy.bis:
Hain ang labing modako kon initon: solid, likido, o gas?

Ang mga solid, likido, ug gas tanan molapad kon initon! Apan ang gas mao ang labing modako, ug ang solid mao ang labing gamay.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: used in digital thermometers, smartphones, and air conditioners to measure temperature electronically
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: plan simple scientific investigations in answering questions, such as 'Do gases (like air) or liquids (like water) have mass?', using appropriate simple science equipment, such as a balance, and a thermometer, with appropriate units
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a thermistor as a temperature-sensing component and mentions digital thermometers, but it does not support planning a simple scientific investigation about whether gases or liquids have mass, nor does it address using a balance, appropriate units, or investigation design. The only connection is the word 'thermometer' and temperature measurement.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A thermistor is a semiconductor whose resistance changes with temperature
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided investigations to infer the relationship among current, voltage, and resistance in assembled series and parallel circuits with varying number of loads and battery
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions resistance changing with temperature, which is tangentially related to electrical resistance, but it does not support guided investigations inferring the relationship among current, voltage, and resistance in assembled series and parallel circuits with varying loads and battery. No circuit assembly, current/voltage measurement, or relationship inference is taught.

copy.en: A thermistor is a semiconductor whose resistance changes with temperature — used in digital thermometers, smartphones, and air conditioners to measure temperature electronically!
copy.tl: Ang thermistor ay isang semiconductor na nagbabago ang resistansya kapag nagbabago ang temperatura — ginagamit sa digital thermometer, cellphone, at aircon para sukatin ang temperatura electronically!
copy.bis: Ang thermistor usa ka semiconductor nga nagbag-o ang resistensya kung magbag-o ang temperatura — gigamit sa digital thermometer, smartphone, ug aircon sa pagsukod sa temperatura electronically!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Your normal body temperature is about 37 degrees Celsius!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify and appropriately use units in simple science activities, such as milligrams (mg), grams (g), kilograms (kg), and degrees centigrade (C)
assignedReviews.reason: The card uses the unit 'degrees Celsius' but does not teach identification or appropriate use of units in simple science activities. It is a factual statement about body temperature, not instruction on units.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Your normal body temperature is about 37 degrees Celsius!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe homeostasis as a state of balance among all the body systems in humans that needs to be maintained for survival and proper functioning; its indicators include body temperature, glucose level, and blood pressure
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions body temperature, which is one indicator of homeostasis, but it does not describe homeostasis as a state of balance among body systems or explain its maintenance. It only states a normal value, providing no direct instructional support for the competency.

copy.en:
What is the normal temperature of the human body?

Your normal body temperature is about 37 degrees Celsius!
copy.tl:
Ano ang normal na temperatura ng katawan ng tao?

Ang normal na temperatura ng katawan ng tao ay mga 37 degrees Celsius!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang normal nga temperatura sa lawas sa tawo?

Ang normal nga temperatura sa lawas sa tawo mga 37 ka degrees Celsius!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In a liquid thermometer, the liquid expands and rises when warm.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use weather instruments to measure and record some of the characteristics of weather during a school day
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the expansion/contraction mechanism of a liquid thermometer, but does not teach using a weather instrument to measure and record weather characteristics during a school day. The thermometer is only mentioned as an instrument, not as a tool for weather measurement.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In a liquid thermometer, the liquid expands and rises when warm.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the uses of various science equipment and materials used in simple activities, such as a ruler, hand lens, scissors, balloons, modeling clay, and cardboard
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes how a liquid thermometer works, not its uses or the uses of science equipment/materials. It does not support describing the uses of various science equipment and materials as required by the competency.

copy.en: In a liquid thermometer, the liquid expands and rises when warm. It contracts and sinks when cold, showing the temperature!
copy.tl: Sa liquid thermometer, lumalaki at umaakyat ang liquid kapag mainit. Umuurong at bumababa ito kapag malamig, kaya naipapakita nito ang temperature!
copy.bis: Sa liquid thermometer, molapad ug mosaka ang liquid kon init. Mokuyos ug mokunsad kini kon bugnaw, mao ang paagi nga mapakita niini ang temperature!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A thermometer measures temperature!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify and appropriately use units in simple science activities, such as milligrams (mg), grams (g), kilograms (kg), and degrees centigrade (C)
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains that a thermometer measures temperature but does not mention or use any units such as degrees centigrade, milligrams, grams, or kilograms. It does not directly support identifying or appropriately using units.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A thermometer measures temperature!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe different science process skills used in performing simple science activities, such as observing, predicting, and measuring using units such as millimeter, centimeter, and meter
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes measuring temperature with a thermometer, which is a science process skill, but it does not describe the skill itself or use units like millimeter, centimeter, or meter. It only shows a measurement outcome, not the process skill or its units.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A thermometer measures temperature!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: plan simple scientific investigations in answering questions, such as 'Do gases (like air) or liquids (like water) have mass?', using appropriate simple science equipment, such as a balance, and a thermometer, with appropriate units
assignedReviews.reason: The card shows that a thermometer measures temperature, which is a piece of equipment mentioned in the competency. However, it does not involve planning a scientific investigation or answering a question about mass. It provides background knowledge about using a thermometer but does not directly support planning an investigation.

copy.en:
How does a thermometer show if water is hot or cold?

A thermometer measures temperature! Its reading rises in hot water and drops in cold water to show you the exact heat.
copy.tl:
Paano ipinapakita ng termometro kung mainit o malamig ang tubig?

Sumusukat ng temperatura ang termometro! Tumataas ang basa nito sa mainit na tubig at bumababa sa malamig na tubig.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagpakita sa termometro kung init o bugnaw ang tubig?

Magsukod sa temperatura ang termometro! Mosaka ang basahon niini sa init nga tubig ug monaog sa bugnaw nga tubig.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Use the formula: °F = (°C × 1.8) + 32.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify and appropriately use units in simple science activities, such as milligrams (mg), grams (g), kilograms (kg), and degrees centigrade (C)
assignedReviews.reason: The competency asks students to identify and appropriately use units in simple science activities, including degrees centigrade. The card teaches a Celsius-to-Fahrenheit conversion formula, which is not the same as identifying or using temperature units in a simple science activity. It shares the temperature-unit vocabulary but does not directly support the stated skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Use the formula: °F = (°C × 1.8) + 32.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the difference between heat and temperature
assignedReviews.reason: The competency is to explain the difference between heat and temperature. The card only gives a temperature scale conversion formula and does not address heat, the distinction between heat and temperature, or any related concept. It is unrelated to the intended subject.

copy.en:
How do you convert Celsius to Fahrenheit?

Use the formula: °F = (°C × 1.8) + 32. For example, normal body temperature 37°C equals 98.6°F!
copy.tl:
Paano i-convert ang Celsius sa Fahrenheit?

Gumamit ng formula: °F = (°C × 1.8) + 32. Halimbawa, ang 37°C na temperatura ng katawan ay katumbas ng 98.6°F!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pag-convert sa Celsius ngadto sa Fahrenheit?

Gamita ang formula: °F = (°C × 1.8) + 32. Pananglitan, ang 37°C nga temperatura sa lawas katumbas sa 98.6°F!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They are written as negative numbers, like minus 5 degrees Celsius!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify and appropriately use units in simple science activities, such as milligrams (mg), grams (g), kilograms (kg), and degrees centigrade (C)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions degrees Celsius but does not teach identifying or appropriately using units in simple science activities (mg, g, kg, °C). It focuses on negative number notation for temperatures, not on unit identification or usage.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: How are temperatures colder than the freezing point written?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card touches on temperature, which is one weather characteristic, but it does not describe air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, humidity, rain, or cloud cover, nor does it help identify basic weather characteristics. It only explains negative temperature notation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: temperatures colder than the freezing point
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change in state, such as solid to liquid to gas
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions freezing point but does not describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change state (solid to liquid to gas). It only explains how to write temperatures below freezing, not the state-change process.

copy.en:
How are temperatures colder than the freezing point written?

They are written as negative numbers, like minus 5 degrees Celsius!
copy.tl:
Paano isinusulat ang temperaturang mas malamig pa sa freezing point?

Isinusulat sila bilang negatibong numero, gaya ng minus 5 degrees Celsius!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagsulat sa temperatura nga mas bugnaw pa sa freezing point?

Gisulat sila isip negatibong numero, sama sa minus 5 ka degrees Celsius!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The thermos cap seals tightly! This traps the heat inside so no warm steam can escape from the top.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify advantageous and disadvantageous examples of conduction, convection, and radiation
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a thermos lid trapping heat and preventing steam escape, which is an everyday example of reducing heat loss. copy.en: The thermos cap seals tightly! This traps the heat inside so no warm steam can escape from the top.
copy.tl: Mahigpit na nakasara ang takip ng termos! Nakakulong nito ang init para walang singaw na makatakas sa itaas.
copy.bis: Higpit nga nakasira ang takup sa termos! Nakakulong niini ang kainit aron walay aso nga makaikyas sa ibabaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: One full liter of liquid is exactly equal to one thousand tiny milliliters!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use measuring cylinders or beakers to measure volume using units, such as milliliters (mL), and liters (L)
assignedReviews.reason: The card provides the conversion between liters and milliliters, which is background knowledge for measuring volume, but it does not involve using measuring cylinders or beakers to measure volume as required by the competency.

copy.en: Did you know? One full liter of liquid is exactly equal to one thousand tiny milliliters!
copy.tl: Alam mo ba? Ang isang buong litro ng likido ay katumbas ng isang libong maliit na mililitro!
copy.bis: Nahibaw-an ba nimo? Ang usa ka bug-os nga litro sa likido katumbas sa usa ka libo ka gamay nga mililitro!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: scientists split all living things into just three giant groups called domains.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the importance of the six-kingdom system and the three-domain system of classification of living things
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that there are three domains in the newest classification. It does not describe the importance of the three-domain system, nor does it mention the six-kingdom system at all. The competency requires describing the importance of both classification systems, so this card provides only a related fact without direct instructional support for the stated skill.

copy.en:
How many main domains does life have?

In the newest classification, scientists split all living things into just three giant groups called domains.
copy.tl:
Ilan ang domain, ang pinakamalaking pangkat ng buhay?

Sa pinakabagong sistema, hinahati ng mga siyentista ang lahat ng buhay sa tatlong pinakamalaking pangkat na tinatawag na domain.
copy.bis:
Pila ka domain, ang pinakadako nga grupo sa kinabuhi?

Sa pinakabag-o nga sistema, gibahin sa mga siyentista ang tanang kinabuhi sa tulo ka pinakadako nga grupo nga gitawag domain.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The three main fossil fuels are coal, oil, and natural gas, which give us lots of energy!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from secondary sources to evaluate how renewable and non-renewable generation of electricity in the Philippines impacts human activities and the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card only names the three fossil fuels and states they provide energy. It does not address generation of electricity, impacts on human activities or the environment, or the Philippine context, which are the core actions of the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The three main fossil fuels are coal, oil, and natural gas, which give us lots of energy!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how increased societal uses of renewable energies could mitigate the effects of global climate change, including how the Philippines could make better use of its plentiful natural resources
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions fossil fuels, which are non-renewable energy sources, but does not discuss renewable energies, climate change mitigation, or Philippine natural resources. It provides no direct instructional support for the competency.

copy.en: The three main fossil fuels are coal, oil, and natural gas, which give us lots of energy!
copy.tl: Ang tatlong pangunahing fossil fuel ay karbon (coal), langis (oil), at natural gas na nagbibigay ng enerhiya!
copy.bis: Ang tulo ka nag-unang fossil fuel mao ang karbon (coal), lana (oil), ug natural gas nga naghatag og enerhiya!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: your body needs Go, Grow, and Glow foods together
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses the need for different food groups (Go, Grow, Glow) to work together, which is a nutrition concept. The competency G3-L-6 requires identifying basic needs of living things such as air, food, water, and shelter. The card does not teach that food is a basic need or address air, water, or shelter; it only mentions food groups, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: One food group alone is not enough — your body needs Go, Grow, and Glow foods together, since each group does its own special job for you.
copy.tl: Hindi sapat ang isang food group lang — kailangan ng katawan mo ang Go, Grow, at Glow nang magkasama dahil may sariling trabaho ang bawat isa.
copy.bis: Dili igo ang usa lang ka food group — kinahanglan sa lawas nimo ang Go, Grow, ug Glow nga magkuyog kay ang matag usa adunay kaugalingong trabaho.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Mixtures are grouped into three by particle size
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that mixtures are classified by particle size into solutions, colloids, and suspensions. It does not describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, nor does it address the uniform/non-uniform distinction required by G6-M-4.

copy.en: Mixtures are grouped into three by particle size: solutions, colloids, and suspensions!
copy.tl: Ang mga mixture ay iniuri sa tatlo ayon sa laki ng particle: solutions, colloids, at suspensions!
copy.bis: Ang mga sagol (mixture) gibahin sa tulo sumala sa gidak-on sa partikulo: solusyon, kolloid, ug suspensyon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Each season lasts for three months as Earth travels around the sun.

assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the duration of seasons and Earth's orbit, not the basic characteristics of weather (air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, etc.) that G4-E-4 targets.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and record changes in the weather during a day or over some days and describe the different types and patterns of weather in the local area
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about seasonal duration, not observing/recording day-to-day weather changes or describing local weather types and patterns.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Each season lasts for three months as Earth travels around the sun.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to locate and describe different types of non-living things found in and around their school, such as rocks, soil, water, air, metals, clouds, rain, and sunlight
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not address locating or describing non-living things such as rocks, soil, water, air, metals, clouds, rain, or sunlight.

copy.en: Each season lasts for three months as Earth travels around the sun.
copy.tl: Tumatagal ng tatlong buwan ang bawat season habang naglalakbay ang Earth sa paligid ng araw.
copy.bis: Ang matag season molungtad ug tulo ka bulan samtang ang Earth nagbiyahe libot sa adlaw.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate proper handling and disposal of materials according to their properties, such as reusing objects, disposing of excess oil into garbage, and recycling paper, plastic or glass

How far away is that lightning strike?

Count the seconds from flash to thunder, then divide by 3. That's your distance in kilometers!
copy.tl:
Gaano kalayo ang kidlat na iyon?

Bilangin ang segundo mula sa kidlat hanggang kulog, tapos hatiin sa 3. Iyon ang layo sa kilometro!
copy.bis:
Unsa ka layo na ang kilat?

Ihapa ang segundo gikan sa kilat hangtod sa dalugdog, unya bahina sa 3. Mao na ang gilay-on sa kilometro!

Want the distance in miles instead?

Just divide the seconds between lightning and thunder by 5. That's how many miles away it is!
copy.tl:
Gusto mo naman ng layo sa milya?

Hatiin mo lang sa 5 ang segundo sa pagitan ng kidlat at kulog. Iyon ang layo sa milya!
copy.bis:
Gusto ba nimo ang gilay-on sa milya?

Bahina lang sa 5 ang segundo tali sa kilat ug dalugdog. Mao na ang gilay-on sa milya!

How fast does the sound of thunder travel?

The sound of thunder travels at about 343 meters per second through the air!

Gaano kabilis ang paglalakbay ng tunog ng kulog?

Ang tunog ng kulog ay naglalakbay sa bilis na halos 343 metro kada segundo sa hangin!
copy.bis:
Unsa ka paspas ang pagbiyahe sa tingog sa dalogdog?

Ang tingog sa dalogdog mobiyahe og mga 343 metros kada segundo sa hangin!

copy.tl: Ang tunog ng kulog ay naglalakbay sa hangin nang mga 343 metro kada segundo (mga 1,235 km/h). Napakabilis!
copy.bis: Ang tingog sa dalugdog mobiyahe sa hangin og mga 343 metros kada segundo (mga 1,235 km/h). Paspas kaayo!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Thunderstorms form when warm, moist air rises quickly and builds tall, giant storm clouds in the sky!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and record changes in the weather during a day or over some days and describe the different types and patterns of weather in the local area
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains a cause of thunderstorms but does not support observing/recording weather changes or describing local weather types/patterns.

copy.en:
What ingredients do you need to bake up a big thunderstorm?

Thunderstorms form when warm, moist air rises quickly and builds tall, giant storm clouds in the sky!
copy.tl:
Anong mga sangkap ang kailangan para gumawa ng isang malaking thunderstorm?

Nabubuo ang thunderstorm kapag mabilis na umaakyat ang mainit at mahalumigmig na hangin at bumubuo ng matataas na ulap!
copy.bis:
Unsa nga mga sangkap ang kinahanglan aron makahimo og dako nga thunderstorm?

Ang unos matawo kung ang mainit ug umog nga hangin mosaka dayon ug maghimo og taas nga mga panganod!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Thunderstorms bring heavy rain, strong wind, and sometimes falling ice called hail!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions rain and wind, which are weather characteristics, but it does not teach identifying basic weather characteristics such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, or cloud cover. assignedReviews.card_evidence: Thunderstorms bring heavy rain, strong wind, and sometimes falling ice called hail!

copy.en: Thunderstorms bring heavy rain, strong wind, and sometimes falling ice called hail!
copy.tl: Ang thunderstorm ay may dalang malakas na ulan, malakas na hangin, at minsan ay yelong bumabagsak!
copy.bis: Ang unos adunay kusog nga ulan, kusog nga hangin, ug usahay nagahulog nga yelo nga gitawag og hail!

copy.tl: Ang garapatang aso ay isa sa pinakakaraniwang garapata sa Pilipinas, madalas itong makita sa balat ng mga aso.
copy.bis: Ang garapata sa iro maoy usa sa labing komon nga garapata sa Pilipinas, kasagaran makita sa panit sa mga iro.

copy.en: On a ticker tape, the space between two dots represents the distance the object traveled during one equal time interval, like one second.
copy.tl: Sa ticker tape, ang pagitan ng dalawang tuldok ay kumakatawan sa distansyang nilakbay ng bagay sa loob ng isang pantay na pagitan ng oras, tulad ng isang segundo.
copy.bis: Sa ticker tape, ang gilay-on tali sa duha ka tuldok nagrepresentar sa distansya nga nalatas sa butang sa sulod sa usa ka pareho nga gidugayon sa oras, sama sa usa ka segundo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Its gravity pulls the sea up and down
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: relate the relative movements of the Earth, Moon, and Sun with the occurrence of tides
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the Moon's gravity causing tides, but does not relate the relative movements of the Earth, Moon, and Sun to the occurrence of tides. It focuses on tidal energy generation, not the astronomical relationships required by the competency.

copy.en: Tidal energy comes from the Moon! Its gravity pulls the sea up and down, and we turn that ocean movement into electricity.
copy.tl: Ang tidal energy ay galing sa Buwan! Ang grabidad nito ay humihila ng dagat pataas at pababa, at ginagawa nating kuryente ang paggalaw ng karagatan.
copy.bis: Ang tidal energy gikan sa Buwan! Ang grabidad niini nagbira sa dagat pataas ug paubos, ug among gihimo nga koryente ang paglihok sa kadagatan.

assignedReviews.reason: The card states that ocean power is renewable and can generate electricity, but it does not evaluate impacts on human activities or the environment, nor does it reference the Philippines or secondary sources. It only touches the broad topic of renewable electricity generation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Rising and falling tides
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: relate the relative movements of the Earth, Moon, and Sun with the occurrence of tides
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions tides but does not relate their occurrence to the relative movements of the Earth, Moon, and Sun. It only notes that tides can spin a turbine, which is about energy generation, not the cause of tides.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: make electricity

assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies the ocean as a source of energy that can make electricity, but the competency focuses on observing and identifying sources and uses of light, sound, and heat energy. copy.en: The ocean's power makes renewable energy! Rising and falling tides and big waves have the force to spin a turbine and make electricity.
copy.tl: Ang lakas ng dagat ay pwedeng gawing renewable energy! Ang pagtaas at pagbaba ng tides at malalaking alon ay puwedeng pumairot ng turbine para sa kuryente.
copy.bis: Ang kusog sa dagat mahimong renewable energy! Ang pagsaka ug pagkanaog sa tides ug dagkong balod adunay kusog nga makapatuyok sa turbine aron maghimo ug kuryente.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Tides reach into river mouths near the sea!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: relate the relative movements of the Earth, Moon, and Sun with the occurrence of tides
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes an effect of tides (saltwater reaching river mouths) but does not relate the relative movements of the Earth, Moon, and Sun to the occurrence of tides. It shares the topic of tides but gives no instructional support for the competency's causal mechanism.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Tides reach into river mouths near the sea!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a coastal river mouth and brackish mangrove water, but it does not identify a local landform/body of water and describe how it influences non-living and living components. The brackish-water observation is too incidental to directly support the competency.

copy.en: Tides reach into river mouths near the sea! At high tide, salty water pushes inland — that's why water in coastal mangroves tastes brackish.
copy.tl: Umaabot ang tides sa bunganga ng ilog malapit sa dagat! Kapag taog, pumapasok ang tubig-alat paloob — kaya maalat ang tubig sa mga bakawan!
copy.bis: Moabot ang tides sa baba sa suba duol sa dagat! Kung taob, mosulod ang tubig-asin paingon sa sulod — mao nga asgad ang tubig sa mga bakawan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: During king tides or spring tides, water sometimes floods low coasts like around Manila Bay
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: relate the relative movements of the Earth, Moon, and Sun with the occurrence of tides
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions spring/king tides and coastal flooding but does not explain the relative movements of the Earth, Moon, and Sun that cause tides. It only names the tidal phenomenon without addressing the astronomical relationship.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: especially when it lines up with a storm or heavy rain!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe some effects of weather disturbances that occur in or near the Philippines
assignedReviews.reason: The card notes that flooding is worse when a high tide coincides with a storm or heavy rain, but it does not describe effects of weather disturbances themselves. The storm/rain is only a contributing factor, not the focus, and no specific weather disturbance effects are described.

copy.en:
Why do some coasts flood during the very highest tides?

During king tides or spring tides, water sometimes floods low coasts like around Manila Bay — especially when it lines up with a storm or heavy rain!
copy.tl:
Bakit binabaha ang ilang baybayin tuwing pinakamataas na taog?

Tuwing king tide o spring tide, minsan umaapaw ang tubig sa mababang baybayin tulad ng paligid ng Manila Bay — lalo na kung sabay sa bagyo o malakas na ulan!
copy.bis:
Ngano nga nalunop ang ubang baybayon kung pinakataas nga taob?

Sa king tide o spring tide, usahay molunop ang tubig sa mubo nga baybayon sama sa palibot sa Manila Bay — ilabina kung dungan sa bagyo o kusog nga ulan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Tides are the slow rise and fall of the whole sea caused by the gravity of the Moon and Sun!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: relate the relative movements of the Earth, Moon, and Sun with the occurrence of tides
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that tides are caused by the gravity of the Moon and Sun, but does not relate the relative movements of the Earth, Moon, and Sun (e.g., alignment, phases, spring/neap tides) to the occurrence of tides. It provides a cause but not the movement relationship required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Waves are made by wind on the surface.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out investigations with water waves in a ripple tank and observe and describe the features of the waves including shape (crests and troughs), size (width and height), and patterns of movement (how they bend, or reflect off walls)
assignedReviews.reason: The card only distinguishes waves from tides and mentions that waves are made by wind. It does not involve ripple tank investigations, observing wave features (crests, troughs, width, height), or patterns of movement (bending, reflection). The content is about tides, not the required wave investigation.

copy.en:
Are tides the same as waves?

No! Waves are made by wind on the surface. Tides are the slow rise and fall of the whole sea caused by the gravity of the Moon and Sun!
copy.tl:
Magkapareho ba ang tides at alon?

Hindi! Ang alon ay gawa ng hangin sa ibabaw. Ang tides ay mabagal na pagtaas-pagbaba ng buong dagat dulot ng gravity ng buwan at Araw!
copy.bis:
Pareho ba ang tides ug balod?

Dili! Ang balod gibuhat sa hangin sa ibabaw. Ang tides mao ang hinay nga pagsaka ug pagkanaog sa tibuok dagat tungod sa gravity sa bulan ug Adlaw!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Tide heights differ by place!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: relate the relative movements of the Earth, Moon, and Sun with the occurrence of tides
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses variation in tide heights due to coast shape and sea depth, but does not relate the relative movements of the Earth, Moon, and Sun to the occurrence of tides. It shares the topic of tides but provides no direct instructional support for the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: because the coast's shape and sea depth affect it
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions coasts and sea depth, which are related to landforms and bodies of water, but it does not identify local examples or describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment. It only notes that coast shape and sea depth affect tide heights.

copy.en: Tide heights differ by place! In some coasts, it rises just a little, but in others, it's huge because the coast's shape and sea depth affect it.
copy.tl: Iba-iba ang taas ng taog sa bawat lugar! Sa iba ay bahagya lang, pero sa iba ay napakalaki dahil naaapektuhan ito ng hugis ng baybayin at lalim ng dagat.
copy.bis: Lainlain ang kataas sa taob sa matag dapit! Sa pipila gamay lang, pero sa uban dako kaayo tungod kay maapektuhan kini sa porma sa baybayon ug lalom sa dagat.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The tiesa (canistel) has soft, orange-yellow flesh just like a cooked egg yolk
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the fruit's flesh and sweetness, not the outer parts of plants (leaves, roots, stems) or their role in water/nutrient uptake. It shares the plant topic but does not support the competency's skill or concept.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The tiesa (canistel) has soft, orange-yellow flesh just like a cooked egg yolk
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions 'soft' and color, which are physical properties, but it describes a fruit's flesh, not a solid material in the sense of the competency (e.g., hard, shiny, stretchable). It does not directly teach describing physical properties of solid materials as intended.

copy.en:
Why is tiesa called 'egg fruit'?

The tiesa (canistel) has soft, orange-yellow flesh just like a cooked egg yolk — that's why it's called 'egg fruit'! It's sweet when ripe.
copy.tl:
Bakit tinatawag na 'egg fruit' ang tiesa?

Ang tiesa o canistel ay may malambot at dilaw-kahel na lamang na parang lutong pula ng itlog — kaya tinatawag itong 'egg fruit'! Matamis ito kapag hinog.
copy.bis:
Nganong gitawag'g 'egg fruit' ang tiesa?

Ang tiesa o canistel adunay humok ug dalag-kahel nga unod nga sama sa giluto nga pula sa itlog — mao nga gitawag kining 'egg fruit'! Tam-is kini kon hinog na.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Tilapia is a cheap fish that gives protein to the food of many Filipinos.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe examples and explain how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet their basic needs
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that tilapia provides protein to Filipinos, which implies humans depend on tilapia for food, but it does not explain how living things depend on one another or on the environment to meet basic needs. It lacks the instructional content of the competency.

copy.en: Tilapia is a cheap fish that gives protein to the food of many Filipinos.
copy.tl: Ang tilapia ay murang isda na nagbibigay ng protina sa pagkain ng maraming Pilipino.
copy.bis: Ang tilapia barato nga isda nga naghatag og protina sa pagkaon sa daghang Pilipino.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: If you know the distance and speed, you find time by dividing distance by speed!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that how far an object moves in a given time is called speed
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches how to compute time from distance and speed (time = distance / speed), but the competency G4-F-3 is about identifying that speed is how far an object moves in a given time. The card does not define speed or state that speed equals distance divided by time; it assumes speed is already known and rearranges the formula to solve for time. This is a related application of the speed concept, not direct instruction for the competency.

copy.en:
How do you figure out the time?

If you know the distance and speed, you find time by dividing distance by speed!
copy.tl:
Paano mo malalaman ang oras?

Kung alam mo ang distansya at bilis, makukuha mo ang oras sa pamamagitan ng paghahati ng distansya sa bilis!
copy.bis:
Unsaon nimo pagkahibalo sa oras?

Kung nahibal-an nimo ang gilay-on ug katulin, makuha nimo ang oras pinaagi sa pagbahin sa gilay-on sa katulin!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Big changes through natural selection don't happen overnight
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe natural selection as the primary mechanism driving evolutionary change
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions natural selection and that evolutionary change takes time, but it does not describe natural selection as the primary mechanism driving evolutionary change, nor does it involve using secondary sources. It only touches on a related fact about the timescale of evolution.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Big changes through natural selection don't happen overnight
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: discuss in small groups important concepts in the theories of evolution, such as variation, heredity, isolation, selection, and adaptation
assignedReviews.reason: The card references selection (natural selection) but does not discuss the important concepts of variation, heredity, isolation, selection, and adaptation as required. It is a single statement about the timescale of evolution, not a discussion of these concepts.

copy.en: Big changes through natural selection don't happen overnight — they usually take thousands or even millions of years!
copy.tl: Ang malalaking pagbabago sa pamamagitan ng natural na seleksyon ay hindi nangyayari kaagad — karaniwan itong tumatagal ng libo-libo o milyon-milyong taon!
copy.bis: Ang dagkong kausaban pinaagi sa kinaiyanhong pagpili dili mahitabo dayon — kasagaran molungtad kini og liboan o milyon ka tuig!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: We measure time in units such as seconds, minutes, and hours!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: measure accurately the distance and time when things move using simple equipment
assignedReviews.reason: The card only names units of time (seconds, minutes, hours). It does not address measuring distance or time when things move, nor using simple equipment, which are the core actions of G4-F-2. Knowing time units is useful background but does not directly teach the measurement skill.

copy.en: We measure time in units such as seconds, minutes, and hours! Tick-tock!
copy.tl: Sinusukat natin ang oras sa mga yunit tulad ng segundo, minuto, at oras!
copy.bis: Atong sukdon ang panahon sa mga yunit sama sa segundo, minuto, ug oras!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: There are about 24 time zones around the world — one for each hour of Earth's rotation!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate the rotation of the Earth on its axis using a globe to explain day and night
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions Earth's rotation as a basis for time zones, but it does not demonstrate rotation using a globe or explain day and night. It only tangentially relates to the competency's topic.

copy.en: There are about 24 time zones around the world — one for each hour of Earth's rotation!
copy.tl: May humigit-kumulang 24 na time zone sa mundo — isa kada oras ng pag-ikot ng Earth!
copy.bis: Adunay mga 24 ka time zone sa kalibutan — usa kada oras sa pagtuyok sa Yuta!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: your body is using its energy to fight off the germs
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that energy is something that can cause change including light, sound, and heat energy
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains tiredness during illness as the body using energy to fight germs. It does not address the competency's focus on energy as something that causes change, nor does it mention light, sound, or heat energy. The only connection is the general word 'energy', which is not sufficient for direct instructional support.

copy.en:
Why do you feel tired when you're sick?

You feel tired when sick because your body is using its energy to fight off the germs!
copy.tl:
Bakit ka napapagod kapag may sakit?

Nakakaramdam ka ng pagod kapag may sakit dahil ginagamit ng katawan mo ang lakas nito para labanan ang germs!
copy.bis:
Nganong maluya ka kon masakit?

Mobati ka og kakapoy kon masakit kay gigamit sa imong lawas ang kusog niini aron labanan ang mikrobyo!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They use titration! It's a lab technique where they add a known solution until neutralization happens, shown by a cool color change.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify common acids, bases, and salts (e.g., hydrochloric acid, sodium hydroxide, and saline solution) using different indicators
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes titration as a method to measure acid/base strength via neutralization and color change, but it does not teach identifying common acids, bases, or salts using indicators. They use titration! It's a lab technique where they add a known solution until neutralization happens, shown by a cool color change.

Gumagamit sila ng titration! Ito ay lab technique kung saan nagdadagdag sila ng known solution hanggang sa neutralization, na nakikita sa pagbabago ng kulay.

Giunsa pagsukod sa mga scientist ang eksakto nga kusog sa usa ka acid o base?

Is a tomato really a fruit?

In science, any plant part with seeds inside is a fruit — so tomato, cucumber, and eggplant are really fruits, even though we call them vegetables!

Sa siyensya, prutas ang anumang bahagi ng halaman na may buto sa loob — kaya ang kamatis, pipino, at talong ay talagang prutas, kahit tinatawag nating gulay!
copy.bis:
Prutas ba gyud ang kamatis?

Sa siyensya, prutas ang bisan unsang bahin sa tanom nga adunay liso sa sulod — busa ang kamatis, pipino, ug talong tinuod nga prutas, bisan tawgon nato silang utanon!

Ilang kilogram ang nasa isang metric ton?

Ang sagot ay malaki! Isang metric ton ay katumbas ng 1,000 kilogram!
copy.bis:
Pila ka kilogramo ang naa sa usa ka metric ton?

Ang tubag dako kaayo! Usa ka metric ton parehas sa 1,000 ka kilogramo!

What body part lets you taste food?

Your tongue is the body part you use to taste food and tell what it tastes like!

Anong bahagi ng katawan ang panlasa mo?

Ang dila ang bahagi ng katawan na ginagamit mo para tikman at malaman ang lasa ng pagkain!

Unsang bahin sa lawas ang imong gamiton para tilawan?

Ang dila mao ang bahin sa lawas nga imong gigamit aron tilawan ug mahibaw-an ang lami sa pagkaon!

A body fossil is an actual part like a bone or shell. A trace fossil, like a footprint or burrow, shows the organism's behavior!

Ano ang pagkakaiba ng body at trace fossils?

Ang body fossil ay aktwal na bahagi tulad ng buto o kabibe. Ang trace fossil, tulad ng yapak o lungga, ay nagpapakita ng gawi ng organismo!
copy.bis:
Unsay kalainan sa body ug trace fossils?

Ang body fossil tinuod nga bahin sama sa bukog o kabhang. Ang trace fossil, sama sa tunob o lungag, nagpakita sa gawi sa organismo!
